sources.title: EV Database: Tesla Model 3 Long Range RWD (Highland, Oct 2024-Oct 2025)

sources.title: KBB: 2026 Tesla Model 3 specs

sources.title: Tesla Model 3 Service Manual (2017-2023): charging rates
sources.notes: States: 240 V outlet max 32 A (about 7.7 kW); "Model 3 accepts up to 48A when equipped with the Long Range Battery" (about 11 kW). No per-year or per-trim table.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Tesla Model 3
sources.notes: Battery section: Fremont cells are Panasonic NCA, Shanghai cells LG NMC (LFP from CATL in both factories). Specs table: RWD 64 kWh / 170 kW; Premium RWD and Premium AWD 78.1 kWh / 250 kW; infobox AC 7.6 kW (32 A) RWD and 11.5 kW (48 A) Long Range. Table columns partly ambiguous.

sources.title: Basenor: Tesla Model 3 legacy charging specs (2017-2023)
sources.notes: RWD (Standard Range reference) 2017-2023: up to 32 A (7.6 kW per Wikipedia); Long Range / Performance up to 48 A (about 11 kW). Does not list SR, SR+ or Mid Range individually.

sources.title: CleanTechnica: Model 3 Standard Range Plus now Supercharges at up to 170 kW
sources.notes: Software 2019.36.1 raised SR+ peak to 170 kW (previously about 100-105 kW); Long Range 250 kW. Pack size only as forum estimates (about 54.5 kWh usable SR+, 74.5 kWh LR).

sources.title: CleanTechnica: Standard Range Model 3 delivered with software-locked range and features
sources.notes: States the 2019 Standard Range is the same physical pack as the Standard Range Plus with range limited in software (220 mi vs 240 mi).

sources.title: Not a Tesla App: Update 2020.24.6.4 release notes (On-Route Battery Warmup)
sources.notes: Release note: vehicle preconditions the battery when navigating to third-party fast chargers in addition to Superchargers; applies to Model S, 3, X and Y. Page does not mention a manual control.

sources.title: Wikipedia: North American Charging Standard
sources.notes: Tesla developed its connector for the Model S in 2012 and used it on all later vehicles including the Model 3; the Supercharger network remains compatible with both the original connector and NACS.
